title: ～のに — “for ～ing” (purpose)
summary: Attached to the dictionary form of a verb, it states a purpose or use: “used for ～ing / useful for ～ing / needed for ～ing / takes ～ to do”.

patterns.gloss: Dictionary form + のに (開けるのに)

body.p: Verb dictionary form + のに means roughly “in order to ～”. You can think of it as the nominalizer の plus the particle に.
It is followed by words about use, usefulness, need, or time and cost: 使う, 役立つ, 便利だ, 必要だ, かかる, いい. Unlike ために, it is not natural for stating the purpose of a deliberate action such as 買う or 行く.

examples.ja: この道具（どうぐ）は缶（かん）を開（あ）けるのに使（つか）います。
examples.romaji: Kono dōgu wa kan o akeru noni tsukaimasu.
examples.tr: This tool is used for opening cans.

examples.ja: この本（ほん）は日本語（にほんご）を勉強（べんきょう）するのに役立（やくだ）つ。
examples.romaji: Kono hon wa Nihongo o benkyō suru noni yakudatsu.
examples.tr: This book is useful for studying Japanese.

examples.ja: 駅（えき）まで行（い）くのに三十分（さんじゅっぷん）かかる。
examples.romaji: Eki made iku noni sanjuppun kakaru.
examples.tr: It takes thirty minutes to get to the station.

pitfalls: This is different from the contrastive のに (“although”); tell them apart by context.
Unlike ために, it does not normally lead into verbs like 行く or 買う (× 勉強するのに日本へ行く).
